title: Foundations of Training Methods
welcome_lead: Discover the toolbox of training methods athletes use to improve.
meta_desc: GCSE PE Methods of Training foundations: continuous, interval, fartlek, circuit.
final_note: Brilliant! You know the main training methods cold.

concepts.def: Periods of work followed by periods of rest.
Speed play — varied pace and terrain.
Stations of different exercises in rotation.
Lifting weights in sets and reps for strength/endurance.
High Intensity Interval Training — short, hard bursts.

walkthroughs.body_html: Continuous training means sustained aerobic work, e.g. a 30-minute jog at conversational pace. It develops cardiovascular endurance. Drawbacks include time required and risk of overuse injury or boredom.

Interval training alternates work and rest, e.g. sprint 100 m then walk 100 m × 8. Adjust work:rest ratios. HIIT is an extreme version — very short, very hard, with brief rest, great for fitness and fat loss.
Fartlek (Swedish for 'speed play') mixes paces and surfaces — great for games players. Circuit training uses 6-10 stations with different exercises, improving general fitness and reducing tedium.
